questions.questionText: When is entropy at its maximum for a two-outcome event?
options: When both outcomes are equally likely (50/50), representing maximum uncertainty
Entropy is always constant regardless of probabilities
When there are more than two possible outcomes
questions.correctAnswer: When both outcomes are equally likely (50/50), representing maximum uncertainty
questions.explanation: Entropy measures uncertainty, and a perfectly balanced 50/50 outcome is maximally unpredictable — you're most "surprised" on average by the result.

questions.questionText: How does log loss (from the logistic regression lesson) relate to cross-entropy?
options: Log loss is cross-entropy applied specifically to a binary classification's two possible outcomes
Cross-entropy only applies to regression, not classification
Log loss is a simplified approximation that ignores probability entirely
questions.correctAnswer: Log loss is cross-entropy applied specifically to a binary classification's two possible outcomes
questions.explanation: Log loss's formula is exactly the cross-entropy formula specialized to two classes, which is why it shares cross-entropy's property of sharply penalizing confident wrong predictions.

questions.questionText: What is the relationship between entropy and decision trees' Gini impurity?
options: They measure completely different, unrelated properties
Both measure how "mixed" or uncertain a group of labels is, and trees can be built by minimizing either one
Gini impurity is only used for regression trees
Entropy can only be computed for continuous values, never class labels
questions.correctAnswer: Both measure how "mixed" or uncertain a group of labels is, and trees can be built by minimizing either one
questions.explanation: Gini impurity and entropy are both impurity measures for a group of class labels — scikit-learn's decision trees support either as the split criterion, and they typically produce similar trees.
